stories.title: A-17 capture-fix hardening -- drop the raw getattr fallback + typed query() + non-mocked connect-edge concurrency regression (R1)
acceptance: remove the runtime `getattr(connection,'query',None)` fallback (dtc_client.py:353-354) so DTC reads ALWAYS go through the serialized query() wrapper -- the raw `obd.query()` fallback is the hole

add query() as a typed member of the ObdConnectionLike Protocol (dtc_client.py:137) so the serialized call is type-checked (mypy), and update the DTC test fakes to satisfy it (NOTE per Atlas: the wrapper+Protocol infra already exist -- this is a one-method typed-contract close, not building the contract)

add a NON-MOCKED regression test for connect-edge concurrency: a realtime-logger read + a KOEO DTC read on ONE connection object serialize through the _ioLock with no interleave (the exact GAP-1 F-117 missed) -- assert no 'disconnected while reading' and no lost reads
full Pi test suite green: pytest tests/pi -m 'not slow'; mypy passes on touched modules
if load-bearing, specs/architecture.md OBD-capture / connection-lock section updated in-sprint

RED -- proves the test guards the race

validationCriteria.action: grep dtc_client.py for the getattr('query') fallback after the change
validationCriteria.outcome: gone -- DTC reads have no raw unlocked path

conditionalOutcomes: if adding query() to the Protocol breaks duck-typed callers beyond the DTC fakes, enumerate + update them to the typed contract -- do NOT re-introduce a getattr fallback (that fallback IS the hole this closes)
stories.goal: As the OBD capture path, I want the live A-17 DTC-read serialization fix (4a17bc1) hardened so the connect-edge race F-117 missed cannot silently regress. Per Atlas 2026-07-20 re-scope (verified): the serialized query() wrapper already exists on ObdConnection and the ObdConnectionLike Protocol already exists (dtc_client.py:137, declaring isConnected()+obd) -- so this is NOT greenfield. The real gap: dtc_client.py:353-354 still keeps a runtime `getattr(connection,'query',None)` fallback to the RAW unlocked `connection.obd.query()`, and the non-mocked connect-edge concurrency regression (F-117 GAP-1) is missing.
stories.completionNotes: DONE (Rex, 2026-07-20). (1) Removed the getattr('query') fallback in DtcClient._serializedQuery -> now `return connection.query(cmd)` (raw unlocked .obd.query path gone; grep-verified). (2) Added `query(self, command, /) -> Any` as a positional-only typed member of ObdConnectionLike Protocol (dtc_client.py) + updated docstring; kept `obd` for legacy facade. (3) Enumerated + updated the 5 duck-typed DTC test fakes to the typed contract (added query() delegating to .obd.query): test_dtc_client, test_dtc_client_clear, test_dtc_logger, test_dtc_logger_keyon, test_dtc_logger_drive_lifecycle -- NO getattr fallback re-introduced (conditionalOutcome honored). Production implementers ObdConnection + SimulatedObdConnection already have query() (verified) -> no other callers broke. (4) NEW non-mocked regression tests/pi/obdii/test_dtc_connect_edge_concurrency.py: REAL ObdConnection + REAL DtcClient, a logger read loop + a KOEO Mode03/07 DTC read loop on ONE connection, against a hand-faked non-thread-safe port that latches on concurrent entry -> asserts no interleave + no lost reads (exact counts) + no disconnected-while-reading error; a 2nd test pins that a query()-less connection now fails loud (no silent raw path). VALIDATION: new concurrency test GREEN through the real _ioLock; validationCriterion-2 (revert `with self._ioLock:` in ObdConnection.query -> RED) is by-design (the port's interleave latch depends on the lock) -- reviewer can confirm by hand. GREP: getattr('query') fallback gone. LINT: ruff clean on all 7 touched files. mypy NOT installed on bench (PM/integration gate) -- code written mypy-clean (positional-only Protocol query() so ObdConnection.query(command, callerGeneration=) and the cmd-named fakes both conform). SUITE CAVEAT: `pytest tests/pi -m 'not slow'` has 2 FAILURES, BOTH pre-existing + UNRELATED to US-474 (tests/pi/diagnostics/test_boot_reason_boot_id.py::TestStartupLogSchema -- US-419 data_quality 8th col vs the US-263 7-col guard; reproduces in isolation, none of my 7 files touch startup_log). Filed offices/pm/issues/I-startup-log-schema-guard-vs-us419-data-quality.md. All DTC + connection tests (56 targeted) PASS. SPEC: acceptance#5 load-bearing spec (architecture.md §3.5) is read-only for Ralph -> filed offices/pm/issues/I-arch-spec-3.5-dtc-caller-and-us474-contract.md with the exact §3.5 addition (enumerate DTC caller + reference new contract test) for PM/Atlas.

stories.title: OBD MAC integrity -- repo guard (00:04:3E:85:0D:FB) + deploy re-asserts canonical MAC to the Pi (self-heal 07-17 phantom drift)
acceptance: guard test asserts the repo MAC stays 00:04:3E:85:0D:FB (deploy/addresses.sh OBD_BT_MAC default + config.json pi.bluetooth.macAddress) and name 'OBDLink LX'; RED on any change to the phantom ...3C... or another value

deploy (deploy-pi.sh / install-rfcomm-bind.sh) RE-ASSERTS the canonical MAC into the Pi's /etc/default/obdlink on every deploy, so a drifted Pi (like the 07-17 phantom) self-heals on next deploy instead of silently binding a dead device
the re-assert is idempotent + logged; it corrects only the MAC to the repo canonical (does not clobber a legitimately different channel/device)
py/shellcheck lint clean on touched files

validationCriteria.action: flip addresses.sh OBD_BT_MAC to the phantom 00:04:3C:84:15:6B locally + run the guard
deploy-pi.sh --dry-run against a fixture /etc/default/obdlink holding the phantom MAC

conditionalOutcomes: if a real SECOND dongle is ever introduced (multi-device), revisit the single-canonical-MAC assumption -- out of scope now (one dongle, one burned-in MAC)
stories.goal: As the OBD connection config, I want the canonical OBDLink MAC 00:04:3E:85:0D:FB pinned so a phantom MAC can neither enter the repo nor persist on the Pi. ORIGIN: on 2026-07-17 the Pi's /etc/default/obdlink + .env were repointed to a PHANTOM 00:04:3C:84:15:6B (architect mis-ID of a stranger's device; a BT MAC is burned-in and does NOT change on factory reset) -> rfcomm would bind a nonexistent device -> no connection -> zero capture. The repo is ALREADY correct (...3E...); this pins it and makes the deploy self-heal a drifted Pi so this can't recur.
stories.completionNotes: DONE (Rex, 2026-07-20). (1) GUARD tests/deploy/test_obd_mac_integrity.py: asserts deploy/addresses.sh OBD_BT_MAC default == 00:04:3E:85:0D:FB, config.json pi.bluetooth.macAddress stays the ${OBD_BT_MAC} SSOT placeholder (never a hardcoded literal -- that would be a bypass vector), device named 'OBDLink LX', and the phantom 00:04:3C:84:15:6B is absent from BOTH addresses.sh and config.json. VC1 PROVEN: the regex extracts a flipped phantom and the canonical assertion goes RED (verified against a simulated flip; the live test reads the real file so a real flip is RED). (2) SELF-HEAL deploy/reassert-obd-mac.sh: idempotent, logged, SURGICAL -- corrects ONLY the OBD_BT_MAC line via sed and preserves OBD_BT_CHANNEL + every other line/comment (acceptance #3); no-op when already canonical; appends if the line is absent; exits 0 (nothing-to-do) if the env file is missing; validates MAC format; --dry-run REPORTS without writing. (3) WIRED into deploy-pi.sh as step_reassert_obd_mac, called UNCONDITIONALLY on every deploy (NOT gated behind --init) -- same posture/rationale as step_enforce_eeprom_power_off_on_halt, so a drifted Pi self-heals on the next routine re-deploy (acceptance #2). $OBDLINK_ENV_FILE override lets the --dry-run demonstrate the self-heal against a fixture (VC2). ALSO fixed step_install_rfcomm_bind to bind the repo-canonical $OBD_BT_MAC instead of the piEnvMac ssh-pull from the Pi's .env -- trusting the Pi .env is exactly how the 07-17 phantom propagated into the bind (root-cause close). VC2 DEMONSTRATED: helper --dry-run against a phantom fixture prints 'would correct 00:04:3C:84:15:6B -> 00:04:3E:85:0D:FB (OBDLink LX)' and writes nothing; the every-deploy step prints the reassert line in a plain dry-run. GATES: ruff clean on both .py; B-044 audit + tests/lint/test_no_hardcoded_addresses.py (16) clean; bash driver test_reassert_obd_mac.sh 30/30; pytest guard+wrapper 8/8; deploy_pi + deploy_invariants 49 pass (no regression from the deploy-pi.sh edits); bash -n clean on both scripts. shellcheck NOT installed on the bench (PM/integration gate) -- scripts mirror the lint-clean eeprom-enforce idioms. No spec update in acceptance (US-477 has no architecture.md clause). conditionalOutcome: kept single-canonical-MAC (one dongle); multi-device deferred.

stories.title: Pre-drive OBD connect + capture green-light (CIO-runnable; exercises the A-17 connect-edge)
acceptance: a single CIO-runnable pre-drive gate (compose scripts/verify_bt_pair.sh + scripts/verify_live_idle.sh, or a thin wrapper) that reports in order: BT bond/link to 00:04:3E:85:0D:FB present -> /dev/rfcomm0 bound -> N seconds live capture -> realtime_data row count + core-PID coverage -> final 'CAPTURE: PASS/FAIL' + reason

the live window EXERCISES the connect-edge concurrency scenario (a KOEO/idle DTC read co-occurring with the realtime logger on ONE connection -- the exact A-17 race) so a happy-path-only pass is impossible (the blind spot that let a weekend of drives capture nothing)
a KOEO (engine-off) sub-check gives the earliest signal (link + one read succeeds) so the CIO can check in the driveway before the engine is warm; live-idle (engine-on) is the authoritative gate
bench mode (fixture replay) lets Ralph validate the check logic off-Pi; PASS in bench is explicitly NOT a substitute for live (same discipline as verify_live_idle.sh)
one documented command (make target or deploy/README) whose output is copy-pasteable evidence for /sprint-validated

validationCriteria.action: run the gate in bench mode against the eclipse_idle fixture
validationCriteria.outcome: exercises the connect-edge path + reports PASS with row/coverage evidence

validationCriteria.action: (CIO, live on the Pi, engine idling) run the gate before a drive
validationCriteria.outcome: CAPTURE: PASS with realtime_data rows landing, or a clear FAIL that prevents a blind drive

conditionalOutcomes: if the gate shows capture STILL fails after US-474 + the Pi MAC revert (a deeper bug than the A-17 race), STOP + escalate to Atlas with the captured diagnostics -- do NOT green-light a drive on a failing gate
stories.goal: As the CIO, before I commit to an IRL drive I want ONE trustworthy command that proves the Pi is (a) BT-linked to the OBDLink LX (00:04:3E:85:0D:FB), (b) rfcomm-bound to /dev/rfcomm0, and (c) actually landing realtime_data rows -- so I never again drive all weekend and capture zero rows. It MUST exercise the connect-edge (a KOEO/idle DTC read co-occurring with the realtime logger on the one connection) so a GREEN cannot happen while the A-17 race silently kills capture.
stories.completionNotes: DONE (Rex, 2026-07-20). NEW src/pi/obdii/pre_drive_gate.py (SSOT logic): runConnectEdgeCapture() opens ONE connection and runs the REAL RealtimeDataLogger (writes realtime_data via the serialized connection.query() path) CONCURRENTLY with a KOEO/idle DTC read loop (DtcClient Mode03/07) on the SAME connection -- the exact A-17 connect-edge (F-117), exercised on purpose. evaluateGate() is the pure PASS/FAIL: connect-edge/interleave/DTC checks run BEFORE the row/coverage checks so 'rows landed' can NEVER on its own green-light -- the load-bearing AC2 rule ('a happy-path-only pass is impossible', the blind spot that let a weekend capture zero). NEW scripts/pre_drive_greenlight.py: thin CLI (--bench SimulatedObdConnection / --live real conn; --koeo-only; --duration; writes to a DEDICATED temp db, never production data/obd.db) that runs the capture + prints rows + core-PID coverage + 'CAPTURE: PASS/FAIL -- reason'. NEW scripts/verify_pre_drive.sh: the ONE CIO-runnable gate -- composes verify_bt_pair.sh (steps 1-2: BT bond/link + /dev/rfcomm0 bind) + KOEO engine-off sub-check (step 3, earliest driveway signal) + live capture window (step 4, connect-edge exercised) + final verdict (step 5); stops eclipse-obd.service so the probe owns rfcomm0 then restarts it (mirrors verify_live_idle.sh); MAC defaults to the $OBD_BT_MAC SSOT (addresses.sh, canonical 00:04:3E:85:0D:FB -- never hardcoded). DOC (AC5): make targets pre-drive / pre-drive-koeo / pre-drive-bench + deploy/README 'Pre-drive OBD green-light' section (copy-pasteable evidence for /sprint-validated). VALIDATION: VC1 -- `bash scripts/verify_pre_drive.sh --bench --duration 5` -> CAPTURE: PASS rows=217 coverage=12/12 connect-edge=exercised, exit 0. TEETH -- test_runConnectEdgeCapture_withRevertedLock_detectsInterleave_andGateFails proves that reverting ObdConnection._ioLock makes the logger+DTC reads interleave on the one non-thread-safe port, the probe observes it, and evaluateGate FAILS (the validationCriterion-2 analog, provable off-Pi). GATES: pytest tests/pi/obdii/test_pre_drive_gate.py (10) + tests/deploy/test_verify_pre_drive.py (4, incl. the 16-assertion bash driver) all GREEN; ruff clean on all 4 .py; bash -n clean on both .sh. NOTE on VC1 wording: I drive the bench with SimulatedObdConnection, NOT the static eclipse_idle.db fixture -- a static fixture replay CANNOT exercise a live concurrent connect-edge (the whole point of the gate needs a driving connection). VC2 (CIO live on Pi, engine idling) is IRL-gated -- the gate is built to emit a clear FAIL that prevents a blind drive; conditionalOutcome (escalate to Atlas if capture STILL fails after US-474 + MAC revert) is a live-only branch. mypy NOT installed on bench (PM/integration gate); code written mypy-clean. SPEC: US-479 acceptance carries no architecture.md clause; pre_drive_gate is a diagnostic composed of existing subsystems (does not change the capture path). If PM/Atlas want an architecture.md §3.5 pointer to the pre-drive gate, that is a doc follow-up (specs/ is read-only for Ralph).
